os_version: macOS 26.5.2 (25F84), Apple Silicon, Chrome 151 via CDP
app: Precision-vs-pixels duel (20 randomized order-console pages) — macOS replication of the Linux cell
channel_setup: campaign/macos/duel-macos.mjs. SAME deterministic page generator and seeds as src/duel.mjs, so the 20 pages are byte-identical to the Linux cell's — this is a true cross-OS replication, not a re-measurement of different material. Viewport pinned to 1280x800 @ deviceScaleFactor=1 via Emulation.setDeviceMetricsOverride so the pixel condition matches Linux exactly.

t1_read_text.detail: Accuracy PARITY, replicated: 18/18 correct from the structured view AND 18/18 from screenshots (n=6 pages x 3 tasks: count-by-status, max-total customer, customer-for-given-order-id). Methodology improved over the Linux cell: the two conditions were answered by TWO INDEPENDENT SUBAGENTS with identical task text, one given ONLY the .view.txt files, the other ONLY the .png screenshots — neither could see the other's evidence, so the parity claim is not contaminated by shared context.

t2_enumerate.detail: Hardened view enumerates every row and button with boxes; whole page, no scrolling.

t5_blind_action.detail: covered in macos-chrome-cdp (incl. the Retina DPR trap)

measurements.notes: n=20 for cost, n=6 (x3 tasks) for paired accuracy. Structured avg 1578 bytes / 391 est-tokens vs screenshot 62110 png bytes / 1366 image-tokens (exact public formula) => 3.49x fewer tokens, 39.4x fewer bytes. Cross-OS replication is essentially exact: Linux measured 1580 bytes / 391 tokens / 3.5x / 36.4x on the same pages — the 2-byte delta comes from macOS system-ui font metrics changing one text wrap. RETINA ADDENDUM (macOS-specific, absent from the Linux cell) — and it does NOT behave the way a naive w*h/750 suggests. Image tokens are charged AFTER the API's automatic downscale (long edge <=2576 px and <=3.588 MP on Opus 4.7+/Sonnet 5/Fable 5/Opus 5; <=1568 px and <=1.15 MP on Opus 4.6/Sonnet 4.6 and earlier). So the SAME 2x Retina capture of this viewport costs 4784 tokens on a high-res model (ratio 12.24x) but only 1534 on a legacy one (ratio 3.92x) — barely more than the 1366 a CSS-resolution shot costs, because the API scales it back down anyway. Sending Retina pixels to a legacy-tier model buys resolution the model never sees and is the one case where the pixel side is NOT punished. Naive w*h/750 would have reported 5462 here; that figure is wrong and was corrected. Helper: src/image-tokens.mjs.

runtime_verification.method: mechanical scoring of both conditions' answers against held-out truth generated by the page generator (never shown to either agent)
runtime_verification.agreement: structured 18/18, pixels 18/18 — parity, replicating the Linux result
